draft.text: You came in to talk about your ongoing left-sided back pain that has been bothering you for some time.
You mentioned that the pain is random and sometimes happens without warning, especially when bending over.
You had a back surgery called a microdiscectomy in 2020, and you have not had any imaging tests since then.
Your doctor is considering further imaging tests like an MRI or CT scan to look at your spine.
You are also encouraged to keep a pain diary and continue stretching as needed.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have had left-sided back pain for some time.
The pain happens randomly and is worse when you bend over.
No new or worsening symptoms like numbness, tingling, or weakness were found during the visit.
Your back pain may be related to your past surgery in November 2020.
You had a procedure for a broken disk that wrapped around your spinal thecal sac.
You may want to consider further imaging like an MRI or CT scan to check your spine.
